## Web Searcher: TSQR CAQR tree on GPU

Research question: "Research state-of-the-art and NOVEL techniques for a FAST BATCHED SQUARE Householder QR factorization on an NVIDIA B200 (sm_100, Blackwell, TF32/tf32x3 tensor cores, CUDA 12.8, Triton 3.6 + Gluon/TLX, PyTorch 2.11), written as CUSTOM kernels (Triton first, CUDA/CuTe DSL for more control — NOT library calls). I have an existing blocked compact-WY implementation at 2388us geomean (rank #5); competitors WITHOUT NVFP4 reach ~1360us (1.3-1.8x faster), so reachable headroom provably exists. I need techniques to BEAT it, and I may need to invent new ones — propose novel combinations, not just a catalog.

EXACT OUTPUT CONTRACT (this is the binding constraint): output must be packed (H, tau) such that a checker computes Q = torch.linalg.householder_product(tril(H,-1), tau), R = triu(H), and requires (in FP64): ||R - Q^T A|| <= 20*n*eps32 * ||A||, ||Q^T Q - I|| <= 100*n*eps32, and tril(Q^T A, -1) ~ 0. So ANY valid FLAT global Householder representation (H, tau) passes — it need NOT match LAPACK bit-for-bit, but Q must be A's true orthogonal factor and the reflectors must compose as ONE global householder_product sequence (per-panel/per-block reflectors that don't compose globally FAIL). Inputs include ill-conditioned, rank-deficient, near-rank-deficient, clustered-singular-value, near-collinear, banded, and row-scaled matrices, so the method must be numerically robust (naive CholeskyQR that squares the condition number FAILS the ill-conditioned cases).

THE BOTTLENECK: after optimizing the trailing-update GEMMs (already at tensor-core roofline / minimal-MMA round-to-nearest precision), the PANEL FACTORIZATION (the tall-skinny n x IB QR with its SERIAL reflector-by-reflector dependency chain) is now ~45% of runtime and is the critical path. The dominant shapes are batch=640/n=512, batch=60/n=1024 (grid-starved: 60 thread-blocks on 148 SMs leaves most idle during the panel), batch=8/n=2048, batch=2/n=4096.

I need, with code-level specificity and URL citations:
1. HOUSEHOLDER RECONSTRUCTION from communication-avoiding QR: the LAPACK xORHR_COL / xUNHR_COL routine and the Ballard-Demmel-Grigori-Hoemmen-Knight (2014/2015) "Reconstructing Householder vectors from TSQR" method. How to make the reconstruction step CHEAP (it is currently O(batch * n^3) and eats the panel savings) — can the reconstruction itself be tensor-core GEMM-heavy and parallel? Exact recurrences.
2. TSQR / CAQR (communication-avoiding QR): the row-block-tree panel factorization that replaces the serial reflector chain with O(log P) tree-reduction, filling idle SMs at grid-starved batch. How to combine TSQR (which gives R + an implicit Q) with ORHR_COL to emit FLAT geqrf-compatible (H, tau). Per-leaf and merge recurrences; how to map the tree to one-CTA-per-row-block on a GPU without O(n) device-wide barriers.
3. PANEL CRITICAL-PATH SHORTENING that is NOT communication-avoiding: the UT-transform / compact-WY-T-only formulation, recursive/divide-and-conquer panel (geqrt3), look-ahead, and any 2023-2026 GPU technique that shortens the serial Householder dependency chain length (not just GEMM-ifies the trailing apply).
4. BATCHED QR specifically: MAGMA batched geqrf, cuSOLVER batched, and any recent (2023-2026) papers on batched small/medium QR on tensor-core GPUs — what algorithm do they use for the panel, and how do they handle the batch=640/n=512 (GPU-saturating) vs batch=2/n=4096 (GPU-starved) regimes differently?
5. MIXED-PRECISION robust QR: tf32x3/error-corrected-TF32 and 3xTF32 emulation for the panel reflector formation (not just the trailing), and iterative refinement / re-orthogonalization schemes that keep flat-(H,tau) FP32 accuracy on ill-conditioned/rank-deficient inputs.
6. A RANKED list of 3-5 DISTINCT, concrete, buildable approaches (each with the key numerical risk and the cheapest decisive experiment to validate it) to shorten the panel critical path while still emitting exact flat (H, tau) — prioritized for the batch=640/n=512 and batch=60/n=1024 regimes that dominate the geomean. Explicitly include any NOVEL combination you can construct from the above primitives, even if not published."

Your angle: **TSQR CAQR tree on GPU** — 
Search query: `TSQR communication avoiding QR GPU reduction tree panel factorization CUDA batched tall skinny CAQR`

## Task
Use WebSearch with the query above (or a refined version). Return the top 4-6 most relevant results.
Rank by relevance to the ORIGINAL question, not just the search query. Skip obvious SEO spam/content farms.
Include a short snippet capturing why each result is relevant.

Structured output only.

I found relevant research on the topics you searched for. Here's a summary of the key findings:

## Communication-Avoiding QR Factorization

Communication Avoiding QR (CAQR) factorization uses the Tall and Skinny QR factorization algorithm (TSQR) for panel factorization. Unlike ScaLAPACK's panel factorization which requires one allreduce operation per column, TSQR requires one allreduce operation per b columns (where b is a block size), dividing the number of communications by b.

## TSQR Algorithm Details

The Tall–Skinny QR (TSQR) algorithm was developed to avoid working with very tall-and-skinny panels, offering improved parallelisation on distributed memory systems and reduced communication by splitting the input matrix into a one-dimensional block row layout, allowing QR factorisations to be performed concurrently on local blocks. In subsequent reduction steps, the intermediate R-factors are grouped into pairs and orthogonalised, repeating this process until the final upper triangular R is obtained.

## GPU Implementation

An implementation of CAQR factorization running entirely on a single GPU shows that the reduction in memory traffic provided by CAQR allows it to outperform existing parallel GPU implementations of QR for a large class of tall-skinny matrices. This QR is done entirely on the GPU using compute-bound kernels, meaning performance is good regardless of the width of the matrix.

## Batching Considerations

Operations can be batched in order to have sufficient amount of data to perform the calculation maximally efficiently on the GPU.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about reconstructing Householder vectors from TSQR:

## Overview

The Tall-Skinny QR (TSQR) algorithm is more communication efficient than the standard Householder algorithm for QR decomposition of matrices with many more rows than columns. However, TSQR produces a different representation of the orthogonal factor and therefore requires more software development to support the new representation, and implicitly applying the orthogonal factor to the trailing matrix in the context of factoring a square matrix is more complicated and costly than with the Householder representation.

## The Solution

The approach shows how to perform TSQR and then reconstruct the Householder vector representation with the same asymptotic communication efficiency and little extra computational cost.

## Key Algorithm Idea

The key idea is that the Householder vectors that represent an orthonormal matrix can be computed via LU decomposition (without pivoting) of the orthonormal matrix subtracted from a diagonal sign matrix. The standard Householder vector representation may be recovered from the implicit TSQR representation for roughly the same cost as the TSQR itself.

## Benefits for 2D QR Algorithms

The algorithm is able to combine two existing approaches for 2D QR factorizations, leveraging the efficiency of TSQR in panel factorizations and the efficiency of Householder-QR in trailing matrix updates.

The search results focus on foundational work from 2013-2015 and don't contain specific information about GPU tensor core implementations or batched QR variants that you mentioned in your query.

results.title: Reconstructing Householder Vectors from Tall-Skinny QR (Ballard, Demmel, Grigori, Hoemmen, Knight — UCB/EECS-2013-175 Tech Report, full PDF)
results.snippet: This is the canonical full-text source for requirement #1 (the exact ORHR_COL / xUNHR_COL recurrence). Key recurrence stated explicitly: the Householder vectors representing an orthonormal Q can be recovered via an UNPIVOTED LU decomposition of (S - Q), where S is a diagonal sign matrix — i.e. Q = householder-reconstruct(LU(S - Q1)). This makes reconstruction GEMM/LU-heavy and parallel rather than a serial reflector chain, and recovers the flat (H,tau) for ~the same cost as TSQR itself. Directly enables emitting LAPACK-geqrf-compatible flat (H,tau) from an implicit TSQR Q — exactly the output contract (Q=householder_product(tril(H,-1),tau)). The tech-report version contains the full derivation and proofs omitted from the conference paper.

results.title: Reconstructing Householder vectors from Tall-Skinny QR — Journal of Parallel and Distributed Computing (2015 journal version, Ballard et al.)
results.snippet: Peer-reviewed 2015 journal version (the citable 'Ballard-Demmel-Grigori-Hoemmen-Knight 2015' the question names).
